questions.prompt: A string has tension \(80\,\mathrm{N}\) and linear density \(0.020\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}\). Find the wave speed.
If the tension in a string is quadrupled while the linear density stays constant, by what factor does the wave speed change?
questions.answer:
Since
\[
v_w\propto \sqrt{T}
\]
quadrupling \(T\) doubles the speed.

questions.prompt: If the linear density of a string is increased by a factor of \(9\) while the tension stays constant, by what factor does the wave speed change?
questions.answer:
Since
\[
v_w\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}}
\]
increasing \(\mu\) by \(9\) reduces the speed by \(3\).

questions.prompt: A string carries waves at \(50\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) under tension \(125\,\mathrm{N}\). Find its linear density.
Two strings are under the same tension. String A has linear density \(0.010\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}\) and string B has \(0.040\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}\). Compare their wave speeds.
questions.answer:
With the same tension,
\[
v_w\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}}
\]
So
\[
\frac{v_A}{v_B}=\sqrt{\frac{\mu_B}{\mu_A}}=\sqrt{\frac{0.040}{0.010}}=2
\]
String A carries waves twice as fast as string B.

questions.prompt: Show from units alone that \(T/\mu\) has the dimensions of speed squared.
questions.answer:
Tension has units
\[
[T]=\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}
\]
Linear density has units
\[
[\mu]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}
\]
Therefore
\[
\left[\frac{T}{\mu}\right]=\frac{\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}}{\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}}=\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}
\]
which is speed squared.

questions.prompt: A string of fixed mass is stretched so its length doubles while the tension quadruples. By what factor does the transverse wave speed change?
questions.answer:
With fixed mass \(M\), doubling the length halves the linear density:
\[
\mu'=\frac{M}{2L}=\frac{\mu}{2}
\]
The new tension is \(T'=4T\), so
\[
\frac{v'}{v}=\sqrt{\frac{T'/\mu'}{T/\mu}}=\sqrt{\frac{4}{1/2}}=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}
\]
So the wave speed increases by a factor of \(2\sqrt{2}\).

questions.prompt: A string has fixed mass \(M\) and original length \(L\). It is stretched to a new length \(\alpha L\). Find the tension required, in terms of the original tension \(T_0\), to keep the wave speed unchanged. Then find the tension required to double the original wave speed.
questions.answer:
With fixed mass \(M\), stretching the string to length \(\alpha L\) changes the linear density to
\[
\mu'=\frac{M}{\alpha L}=\frac{\mu_0}{\alpha}
\]
Original speed:
\[
v_0=\sqrt{\frac{T_0}{\mu_0}}
\]
New speed:
\[
v'=\sqrt{\frac{T'}{\mu'}}=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha T'}{\mu_0}}
\]
To keep the speed unchanged, set \(v'=v_0\):
\[
\alpha T'=T_0
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
T'=\frac{T_0}{\alpha}
\]
To double the speed, require \(v'=2v_0\), so
\[
\frac{v'^2}{v_0^2}=4=\frac{\alpha T'}{T_0}
\]
Hence
\[
T'=\frac{4T_0}{\alpha}
\]
